validated_results.title: Adaptive-mixture-categorization (AMC)-based g-computation and its application to trace element mixtures and bladder cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: a Participants were 265 non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) cases and 353 controls of the New Hampshire Bladder Cancer Study.
sample_size.location: Methods and materials / Dataset and pre-processing for the application of real data, paragraph 3; total_n derived from reported group counts 265 + 353 = 618

cases.excerpt: a Participants were 265 non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) cases and 353 controls of the New Hampshire Bladder Cancer Study. b “Former smokers” quit smoking more than 1 year before they were diagnosed as cases or selected as controls.
cases.location: Methods and materials / Dataset and pre-processing for the application of real data, paragraph 3

effect_size.excerpt: We observed an inverted U-shaped relationship between toenail zinc concentrations and risk of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: relative to low-level zinc, medium-level zinc had a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.25), but an inverse association that was not significant for high-level zinc (β = − 0.30; 95% CI − 0.41 to 0.01).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We observed an inverted U-shaped relationship between toenail zinc concentrations and risk of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: relative to low-level zinc, medium-level zinc had a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.25), but an inverse association that was not significant for high-level zinc (β = − 0.30; 95% CI − 0.41 to 0.01).

p_value.excerpt: medium-level zinc had a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.25)

comparison.excerpt: medium-level (116.7–145.5 μg/g) vs. low-level (39.5–116.2 μg/g) of toenail zinc had a statistically significant positive association with bladder cancer risk.
